title: Machine Learning Predicts Acute Kidney Injury in Hospitalized Patients with Sickle Cell Disease.
summary: XGBoost applied to minute-level bedside vital-sign streams predicted acute kidney injury up to 12 hours before onset in hospitalized sickle-cell patients. The reviewed source supports this bounded result; external generalization, causal effects, and sustained operational impact remain unestablished where the source reports retrospective or internal evaluation.
ai_technology: The classifier uses five minute-sampled physiologic streams from bedside monitors.
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: In 1,178 filtered encounters across five hospitals, AUROC was 0.91 at 12 hours and 0.82 at 48 hours before AKI.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective regional-network evaluation with limited AKI cases; abstract and full paper note generalizability limits and no intervention outcome.
evidence.ai_role: The classifier uses five minute-sampled physiologic streams from bedside monitors.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
